summary: Security review of the /dashboard skeleton-flash fix (page.tsx -> async server component reading the firebaseToken cookie + verifyIdToken, new DashboardBody.tsx client half, layout.tsx deleted). No critical or high findings; nothing blocks merge. All six review questions answered with empirical evidence rather than reasoning where it was possible to do so. (1) verifyIdToken parity: src/lib/firebaseAdmin.ts exports exactly one verifyIdToken (a thin `adminAuth.verifyIdToken(token)`); requireAuth.ts:14,52 imports that same symbol, and so do settings/page.tsx:2,14 and the new dashboard/page.tsx:3,35. There is no second/looser verification path anywhere in the tree. Same options on both sides (neither passes checkRevoked), so the new call is byte-for-byte the hardened path, not a fork. (2) Cookie pattern vs /settings: structurally identical — `const cookieStore = await cookies(); const token = cookieStore.get("firebaseToken")?.value; if (token) { const decoded = await verifyIdToken(token); ... }` inside one try/catch with an empty catch. Presence is never trusted: the token is passed to verifyIdToken and every downstream read is keyed on `decoded.uid`. Proved this live rather than by inspection: started the existing production build (`next start -p 3999`) with throwaway Firebase env, forged a structurally valid RS256 JWT (correct iss/aud/exp, `sub`/`user_id` = victim-uid-123, `email` = victim@example.com, garbage signature) and requested /dashboard with it as the firebaseToken cookie. Result: 200 with `initialData\":null` in the RSC flight payload, zero occurrences of victim-uid-123 and zero of victim@example.com in the HTML. A presence-only check would have leaked both. The proxy.ts presence-only guard (formerly middleware.ts; matcher /dashboard/:path*) still 307s to /auth/signin when the cookie is absent, unchanged, and is still not the access-control layer. (3) CROSS-USER CACHE LEAK — the headline item — clear. Every one of the five reads is request-scoped and uid-keyed: prisma.user.findUnique({where:{id: decoded.uid}}), getUserFreeClimbRecord / getUserClimbReplays (src/db/climb.ts, plain uncached prisma queries), getDuelStats / getRecentDuelsForUser (src/db/duel.ts, plain uncached). The only unstable_cache users in src/db are topFreeClimbers and topDuelStats, and the only React cache() user is getGlobalClimbStats — none is on this path. `decoded` is a local const inside the async request function; there is no module-level or cross-request memo of a uid anywhere in the new code. No `revalidate` export, no ISR, no unstable_cache, no force-static. Measured the actual response headers on the built server: /dashboard returns `Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate` — byte-identical to /settings on the same server, and matching Next's getCacheControlHeader() revalidate===0 branch (node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/cache-control.js:14). .next/server/app/dashboard/ contains only page.js (no .html/.rsc/.meta/.segments artifacts), i.e. nothing personalised is written at build time, consistent with the `f` route-table entry the SE and verifier both measured. OLD version confirmed leak-free for a different reason: `git show HEAD:app/app/dashboard/page.tsx` starts with "use client" and contained no server-resolved data at all, so the statically prerendered `o` HTML was a pure shell. NEW version is per-request and explicitly no-store. Also verified the page is still noindex after the layout.tsx deletion: the live HTML carries `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow"/>`, and cross-origin read of the now-PII-bearing HTML is blocked by `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` (present on the response) plus same-origin policy; SameSite=Lax means the cookie rides top-level navigations but the response body stays unreadable to the initiator. (4) Failure mode is genuinely all-or-nothing. `initialData` is only assigned after `await Promise.all([...])` fully resolves; the object literal is built from already-settled values. Four of the five reads carry their own `.catch()`; the fifth (prisma.user.findUnique) does not — exactly matching /api/dashboard/route.ts:43-46 — so if it rejects, Promise.all rejects, control jumps past the assignment to the outer catch, and initialData stays null. TypeScript's DashboardData requires every field, so a partially-populated object is not constructible here. No path renders one user's data next to a failure. (5) Data-exposure diff: the server-rendered payload is a strict SUBSET of what GET /api/dashboard already returns to the same browser. Field-for-field identical for user{id,email,username,betaJoined}, freeClimb, replays and recentDuels; duelStats is narrowed to {wins,losses,current_streak,best_streak}, dropping user_id and updated_at that the API route passes through raw. So this is a pure rendering-timing change that is marginally stricter than the status quo. replayToken inside replays is a shareable replay encoding already rendered publicly on CreatorProfile.tsx, not a credential. The raw firebaseToken is never echoed into the HTML (grepped the live response: 0 hits). (6) WalletCard/BetaBanner null-token paths are cosmetic-only and fire no requests: WalletCard.refresh() early-returns on !token so /api/wallet is never called; useClaimDailyChips.claim() early-returns on !token AND the claim button is not rendered at all because dailyClaimVisibility(null, 'idle').showClaim === false while wallet is null; BuyCreditsModal is double-guarded (button `disabled={... || !token}` and handleBuy's `if (!token ...) return`), so no Bearer-empty POST to /api/credits/checkout is reachable; BetaBanner remains behind the `token && <BetaBanner token={token} />` guard. The refresh useEffect depends on [refresh] which depends on [token], so it runs exactly once more when the token arrives — one fetch, no retry loop, no 401 storm, no rate-limiter pressure. Checked the other newly-early-mounting children too: Navbar delegates auth to NavbarAuth which itself returns a skeleton while `loading`, so AccountMenu (the only other token-fetching child, /api/settings) does not mount during authLoading; CreatorPageBand, DuelRecordCard, FreeClimbCard, ClimbReplaysSection and DuelReplaysSection issue no requests at all. Secret scan of the full diff plus both new files: clean. `pnpm audit` in app/: 4 pre-existing advisories (1 high deepmerge-ts via the prisma CLI config loader, moderate uuid via @capacitor/cli, moderate fflate via @vercel/og/satori) — none introduced by this change (no dependency edits; the diff touches exactly app/app/dashboard/page.tsx and deletes app/app/dashboard/layout.tsx), and none on a request-handling path reachable from /dashboard. Confirmed /api/dashboard/route.ts, requireAuth.ts, firebaseAdmin.ts and authCookie.ts have zero diff. Read-only review: I changed no files, committed nothing, pushed nothing; the throwaway server was stopped and the scratch key left outside the repo.
goal: Security-review the /dashboard server-side payload resolution: confirm verifyIdToken parity with the hardened auth paths, confirm the cookie read performs real verification rather than trusting presence, rule out cross-user PII leak via shared/render caching, confirm the try/catch failure mode is all-or-nothing, diff newly server-rendered fields against the existing API response, and confirm the null-token child render paths are harmless.

findings.issue: verifyIdToken is called without `{ checkRevoked: true }`, so a session revoked server-side (adminAuth.revokeRefreshTokens) stays renderable until the ID token's own exp, up to ~1 hour. The firebaseToken cookie's 7-day Max-Age does NOT widen this window — verification still enforces exp, which I confirmed empirically (a forged token with a valid exp but a bad signature yields initialData=null).
findings.reproduction: Revoke a user's refresh tokens via the Admin SDK, then reload /dashboard within the unexpired ID token's lifetime with the still-present firebaseToken cookie. The page renders that user's data.
findings.fix: No action for this change — it is exact parity with requireAuth(), which every existing authenticated API route already relies on. If this window is ever deemed unacceptable it must be closed in firebaseAdmin.ts for all callers at once, not forked here. Filed as info, not a regression.
findings.falsePositiveNote: Downgraded from a potential finding because the attack requires already possessing the victim's unexpired ID token, which is itself the bearer credential for /api/dashboard — no privilege escalation over the pre-change state.

findings.owasp: A09 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
findings.issue: The catch body is empty (comment only). Unlike GET /api/dashboard, which does `console.error("[GET /api/dashboard]", error)` on the DB-failure path and `console.error("[requireAuth] Token verification failed")` on the auth path, the new SSR path emits nothing at all. A persistent server-side failure (Firebase Admin degradation, Prisma pool exhaustion) would silently downgrade every /dashboard to the client fallback with zero server-side signal.
findings.reproduction: Make verifyIdToken or prisma.user.findUnique throw in production; observe /dashboard quietly serving initialData=null with no log line attributable to the page.
findings.fix: Optional, non-blocking: log the error constructor name (not the token, not the uid) in the catch, e.g. `console.error("[dashboard/page] initialData unresolved:", err instanceof Error ? err.name : "unknown")`. Do NOT log the token or the decoded claims. Note this would deviate from the /settings precedent, so it is a judgement call for the reviewer/orchestrator, not a security requirement — detection is partially preserved because the client fallback immediately calls /api/dashboard, which does log.
findings.falsePositiveNote: Not raised higher: the failure is fail-closed (no data rendered), so the missing log costs observability, not confidentiality or integrity.

findings.issue: `import { verifyIdToken } from "../../src/lib/firebaseAdmin"` is module-level, and firebaseAdmin.ts throws at module-evaluation time when FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID / FIREBASE_CLIENT_EMAIL / FIREBASE_PRIVATE_KEY are unset. That throw happens OUTSIDE the try/catch, so a misconfigured deploy 500s /dashboard instead of degrading to the client fallback the comment promises.
findings.reproduction: Deploy with FIREBASE_PRIVATE_KEY unset; GET /dashboard returns 500 rather than the skeleton fallback.
findings.fix: None required. Identical to /settings and to every API route that imports firebaseAdmin, and it is a deploy-configuration failure rather than an attacker-controllable condition. Recorded so nobody later reads the catch block as covering all failure modes.
findings.falsePositiveNote: No constructable attack path — the precondition is a broken deployment, not attacker input.

findings.issue: The CSP has no `frame-ancestors` directive; clickjacking/framing protection rests solely on `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`. This matters slightly more now that /dashboard's HTML carries a user's email, uid, climb records and duel stats instead of an empty shell.
findings.reproduction: Not exploitable on current browsers — I confirmed X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN is present on the live /dashboard response, which blocks cross-origin framing everywhere frame-ancestors would.
findings.fix: Pre-existing hardening suggestion for a future repo-wide change, not for this PR: add `frame-ancestors 'self'` to the CSP array alongside the existing X-Frame-Options.
findings.falsePositiveNote: Downgraded to info: X-Frame-Options already blocks the attack in every browser that matters, so there is no constructable framing path today.

findings.issue: `pnpm audit` reports 4 advisories: high deepmerge-ts@7.1.5 (GHSA-ggr8-5vv4-36mx, via @prisma/client > prisma > @prisma/config), moderate uuid@7.0.3 (via @capacitor/cli > xcode), moderate fflate@0.7.3 (via @vercel/og > satori).
findings.fix: Out of scope for this change: the diff adds no dependencies (it touches only app/app/dashboard/page.tsx plus the layout.tsx deletion). deepmerge-ts and uuid are CLI/build-time only; fflate's unzipSync path is not reached from /dashboard. Track separately if the orchestrator wants a dependency-refresh cycle.
findings.falsePositiveNote: None of the three is reachable from any request path this change introduces.

learnings.insight: A page that flips from statically prerendered to dynamic because it now server-renders personalised data can be checked for cross-user cache leakage empirically, without a database or real credentials, in about two minutes: start the existing production build with throwaway Firebase env and a dead DATABASE_URL (`next start -p <port>`), then curl the route. Next 16 emits `Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate` for any route whose cacheControl.revalidate is 0 (node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/cache-control.js), and on this repo /dashboard and /settings returned byte-identical headers. Reading Next internals or reasoning from the `f` route-table marker is weaker evidence than the measured header — the route table tells you the render mode, not what the CDN will do with the response.
learnings.action: For any change that moves personalised data into SSR/RSC output, measure the live Cache-Control (and X-Frame-Options, and the robots meta) with `next start` + curl against the already-built .next, and compare against a known-good sibling route. Do not accept the build route table alone as cache-safety evidence.

learnings.insight: The decisive test for 'does this cookie path really verify, or does it trust presence?' is a forged-but-well-formed token, not a garbage string. A garbage cookie value fails at parse and proves nothing about signature checking. Forging an RS256 JWT with correct iss/aud/exp and an attacker-chosen `sub`/`user_id`/`email`, then grepping the rendered HTML and RSC flight payload for those exact attacker-chosen values, distinguishes real verification from presence-only in one request. On /dashboard this produced `initialData\":null` and zero occurrences of the forged uid or email.
learnings.action: When reviewing any new server-side cookie-derived identity, mint a structurally valid forged JWT carrying a distinctive uid/email, request the route with it, and assert those strings are absent from the response body. Keep the forged-token probe alongside the usual missing/expired-token cases.

learnings.insight: Deleting a route segment's layout.tsx that existed only to carry `metadata` silently removes the page's noindex unless the Metadata export genuinely lands on the new server page. That is a confidentiality-relevant regression for an authenticated page, and neither typecheck nor lint would catch it — nothing imports a metadata export. Here it was done correctly, and I confirmed it at the HTTP layer rather than in source: the live /dashboard HTML still contains `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow"/>`. Note that next.config.js only sets the X-Robots-Tag header for /admin and /api/admin, so /dashboard's noindex depends entirely on that meta tag.
learnings.action: Any time a layout.tsx or page-level Metadata export moves or is deleted on an authenticated route, verify the rendered `<meta name="robots">` in the actual response, not the source. If a route's noindex matters, consider an X-Robots-Tag entry in next.config.js headers() so it cannot be lost by a component refactor.

learnings.insight: Narrowing duelStats server-side to the four fields DuelRecordCard actually reads made the server-rendered payload a strict subset of what GET /api/dashboard already returns (the API route still passes the raw Prisma DuelStats row, including user_id and updated_at, straight to NextResponse.json). That is the right shape for a rendering-timing change: the security question becomes trivially answerable — 'is the new payload a subset of the old one?' — instead of requiring a field-by-field exposure argument.
learnings.action: When moving an existing API payload into RSC output, narrow at the server-component boundary to exactly what the child components read. It makes the exposure review a subset check. Consider applying the same narrowing to /api/dashboard's duelStats so the two paths converge on the lean shape.

learnings.insight: Security review of the /dashboard SSR change: 0 critical, 0 high, 1 low (missing log in the SSR catch block), 4 info (checkRevoked parity, module-level firebaseAdmin import outside the try/catch, missing CSP frame-ancestors, 3 pre-existing audit advisories). Diff scope: 1 file modified, 1 deleted, 0 dependency changes. Secret scan clean. The four protected auth files (/api/dashboard/route.ts, requireAuth.ts, firebaseAdmin.ts, authCookie.ts) have zero diff.
learnings.action: No loop-back required; proceed to qa-acceptance. The single low finding is an optional observability improvement, not a merge blocker.
